data.title: Agent Intent Manipulation — Purchase Divergence from User Intent
data.description: Detects transactions initiated by AI agents where the product or service purchased diverges significantly from the user's stated intent or historical purchasing patterns, or where the receiving merchant is flagged as high-risk. This rule targets Phase 3 (Positioning) of agentic commerce fraud, where threat actors manipulate agent purchasing intent to redirect transactions to attacker-controlled merchants or execute purchases that do not reflect the consumer's actual desires. Key indicators include purchases in product categories the user has never engaged with, transactions at merchants created within the last 30 days, transaction amounts exceeding 3x the user's historical average, and merchants with elevated risk scores.

enrichment_required.source: Behavioral analytics enrichment (user spending baseline comparison)
Behavioral analytics enrichment (purchase history category matching)
Merchant profiling enrichment (merchant onboarding date lookup)
Merchant risk scoring enrichment (fraud risk model)

falsepositives: Users exploring new product categories via agent for the first time
Legitimate purchases from newly launched merchants or startups
Gift purchases in categories outside user's typical patterns
Agent executing user-directed purchases at premium pricing (luxury goods)
